//: Typecheck-only view of server/, covering what `tsconfig.json` cannot.
`tsconfig.json` is the BUILD config: `rootDir: ./src` and `include: [src/**/*]`,
so `scripts/**` and `qa/**` are compiled by nothing and checked by nothing.
That is not theoretical. `qa/eviction-check.mts` called
`startIdleEviction(repo, root.url, 200, 80)` against a five-parameter
signature, binding the residency to `200` and leaving `sweepMs` at its 60 s
default, so no sweep could occur inside the 1 s the check waits: it reported
FAIL on every run and nothing said so. Two scripts called
`synchronizer.removeDocument`, which does not exist in the installed
automerge-repo, behind an `as unknown as` cast.
Do NOT widen `tsconfig.json`'s own `include` instead: its `rootDir` is `./src`,
so anything outside breaks `npm run build`. Hence a second, emit-less config
with a wider root.
Two scripts are excluded, and the reason is structural rather than a waiver:
they import CLIENT source across the package boundary (`../../src/lib/...`)
with TypeScript extensions, which only `tsx` resolves. Checking them here
would pull the browser module graph into a NodeNext program it was never
written for. They stay uncovered; that is a smaller hole than the one this
file closes, and it is named here rather than left to be discovered.
`exclude` REPLACES the parent's, it does not merge with it, so
`src/**/*.test.ts` is repeated below on purpose. Dropping it pulls the whole
test suite into this program and reports 184 pre-existing errors that have
nothing to do with what this file is for — a checker that reports 184 things
nobody is going to fix is a checker nobody runs.
Run: cd server && npm run typecheck:all
//files: A 'files' entry is NOT filtered by 'exclude', which is the only way to
typecheck ONE test file while the other 200 stay out.
The seam test carries a '@ts-expect-error' asserting that
'delete cachedHandles(repo)[id]' is a TS2542. That is the ONLY thing in the
project that catches deleting from the throwaway Record the getter rebuilds:
a syntax-only lint rule cannot follow a local alias, and four of the six
vitest transpiles without typechecking, so that assertion was pure decoration
until this line existed. A mutation run proved it rather than assuming it:
dropping 'Readonly' from the return type left the whole suite green.
